title: ElevenLabs Dubbing vs. HeyGen Video Translation
summary: Compare ElevenLabs Dubbing and HeyGen Video Translation by audio exports, lip sync, translated script review and cost per language.
body_markdown:
Start with ElevenLabs Dubbing when you need a translated audio file for an existing edit. Start with HeyGen Video Translation when you need to translate the speaker and deliver a video with matching mouth movement in one workflow. If a translator or voice actor has already supplied approved audio, you can go straight to a lip-sync tool with your original footage.

ElevenLabs documents[Dubbing v2 output as one lossless audio file](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/dubbing/which-file-formats-are-supported-by-dubbing) . Its older Dubbing Studio lists separate speaker WAVs and timeline data.[ElevenLabs says that Studio is in maintenance mode](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/products/dubbing/dubbing-studio) , so confirm that the export you need is available for the version you’ll actually use. If the original edit has a multichannel mix or the video preview changes resolution, bring the audio into your original project and finish the delivery there.


## Check the mouth, captions and on-screen text separately


HeyGen’s[Video Translation guide](https://help.heygen.com/en/articles/10029081-how-to-get-started-with-video-translation) documents Audio Only for revoicing without lip sync, Speed for simpler front-facing clips, and Precision for harder angles or speaker switches. Its Proofread feature is plan-gated. If a reviewer needs to sign off on the exact words before generation, check that they can access that feature or approve the script elsewhere first.


Check titles, screenshots, labels and burned-in captions in your source video. HeyGen does not translate text embedded in the image through Video Translation. Replace that material in the editing project and build captions from the final approved recording so the displayed text matches what the speaker says.


## Budget one complete language first


ElevenLabs[charges for each source minute in each target language](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/dubbing/how-much-does-dubbing-cost) . The applicable credit rate depends on the model. HeyGen’s guide lists 4 credits per minute for Audio Only, 6 for Speed and 10 for Precision. Those are HeyGen’s credits. Use each provider’s own quote, allowance and renewal terms when you compare cash cost.


Run one language through review before committing to the rest. Budget time for glossary fixes, rerecording, caption corrections and another render if the first file misses the brief. Start with the hardest spokesperson shot and check a brand name, a number and a cut where you can plainly see the speaker’s mouth. Then confirm the final export fits the timeline and delivery spec.


## If the translated recording is already approved


Open[Magic Hour Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) , add the original face video and the approved audio, and line up the start of the selections. Magic Hour’s[timing guide](https://help.magichour.ai/en/articles/15011107-lip-sync-free-tool-vs-create-modes-limits-timing-and-troubleshooting) says the shorter selection determines output length. Check both selections before submitting and review the mouth movement against the completed audio.


[Watch the walkthrough on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8GR0xkxrZYM) .
